> **Proposed API.** This guide follows `docs/api-vision.md`, not the current
> implementation. Code is deliberately non-executable and was not run.
> Scripted replies below are teaching data, not provider results.

A tool call asks your application to do something. It does not give a model
permission to choose arbitrary R functions or run arbitrary code.

The proposed interface keeps four separate steps visible: describe a tool,
receive calls, run allowed work, and append results to the next request.

## Keep the function and its declaration separate

Here is a small local function. It looks up fixed readings, not live weather:

```r
library(lm15)

weather <- function(city) {
  if (!is.character(city) || length(city) != 1L || is.na(city)) {
    stop("city must be one string.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  readings <- c(Montreal = "18 degrees C, clear", Oslo = "12 degrees C, rain")
  if (!city %in% names(readings)) {
    stop("No reading is available for that city.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  unname(readings[[city]])
}
```

Declare its input using an explicit JSON Schema:

```r
weather_tool <- function_tool(
  "weather",
  description = "Look up a reading for Montreal or Oslo.",
  parameters = json_object(
    type = "object",
    properties = json_object(
      city = json_object(
        type = "string",
        enum = as_json_array(c("Montreal", "Oslo"))
      )
    ),
    required = as_json_array("city"),
    additionalProperties = FALSE
  )
)
```

A JSON Schema describes allowed fields and values. It does not make model
output trustworthy: the function still checks its inputs.

`as_json_array()` makes conversion of an R vector explicit. The package does
not guess array shape when serializing a value. Nor does it infer a complete
input schema from R argument defaults. The declaration stays visible, and the
application keeps the function to execute.

## Receive calls as data

```r
req <- request(
  "demo-model",
  message_user("What is the weather in Montreal and Oslo?"),
  tools = list(weather_tool)
)

first_reply <- response(
  "demo-model",
  message_assistant(list(
    tool_call_part("call_montreal", "weather", input = json_object(city = "Montreal")),
    tool_call_part("call_oslo", "weather", input = json_object(city = "Oslo"))
  )),
  "tool_call"
)

client <- fake_lm(list(
  first_reply,
  response("demo-model", message_assistant("Montreal is clear; Oslo has rain."), "stop")
))

answer <- complete(client, req)
calls <- tool_calls(answer)
```

The response contains two calls, each with an ID, name and input. Printing it
should show the count and ending without dumping those inputs. Read them
explicitly when deciding what to execute:

```r
vapply(calls, function(call) call$name, character(1))
response_text(answer)
```

The scalar text view is `NULL`: this response asks for tools. It is not an
empty answer, and it must not become an empty string merely to fit a column.

## Execute an explicit allowlist

```r
run_call <- function(call) {
  if (!identical(call$name, "weather")) {
    stop("The requested tool is not available.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (!identical(names(call$input), "city")) {
    stop("weather requires exactly one input named city.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  weather(call$input$city)
}

replies <- lapply(calls, function(call) {
  output <- run_call(call)
  message_tool(call$id, output, name = call$name)
})
```

`message_tool()` creates a tool message from the result. It does not execute
anything itself. The IDs preserve the connection between each requested call
and the result you chose to return.

Do not replace the allowlist with unrestricted `get(call$name)`,
`eval(parse())`, or shell execution. A more powerful application may need
approval rules and permissions; those belong to the application, not a hidden
lm15 dispatcher.

## Append the exchange without rebuilding its contents

```r
next_req <- req |>
  append_messages(answer$message) |>
  append_messages(replies)

final <- complete(client, next_req)
response_text(final)
```

Both append operations are local value transformations. The first preserves
the complete assistant message, including continuation data. The second
appends a flat list of tool messages. Neither sends a request or changes `req`.
Only the next `complete()` asks the client to perform more work.

This example answers both calls before making the next model call. A real
application should do the same unless it has an explicit alternative protocol.
It should not silently omit a failed call or replace the assistant message
with its display text.

When you need exact control over the parts in a single tool message, the
lower-level constructors remain available:

```r
parts <- list(
  tool_result_part("call_montreal", list(text("18 degrees C, clear")), name = "weather"),
  tool_result_part("call_oslo", list(text("12 degrees C, rain")), name = "weather")
)
one_message <- lm15::message("tool", parts)
```

That is an explicit alternative representation, not a new tool-loop API.
The common path uses role helpers; the exact-type path exposes parts directly.
Qualifying `lm15::message()` also distinguishes it from R's diagnostic
`base::message()`.

## Choose error output, rather than leaking an exception

```r
unavailable <- message_tool(
  "call_missing",
  "No reading is available for that city.",
  name = "weather",
  is_error = TRUE
)
```

This returns a deliberate error message to the model. It is different from an
R failure that your application should stop and handle. Do not convert every
caught exception into tool output: exception details can contain secrets or
information the model does not need.

An empty output is also deliberate: `message_tool(id, "")` contains an empty
text part. It is not a message with no content parts.

## The application still owns the loop

The improved syntax removes list-editing repetition, not policy decisions.
Before another completion, your application still decides whether the calls
are allowed, their arguments are valid, every call has a result, and another
request is within its budget.

There is no automatic retry, execution loop, history truncation, or summary of
older messages. The complete request remains available to inspect and save.
For tabular work, [keep those objects in list columns](data-workflows.html).
